Hits the corner of the service box.
Both players with unimpressive 1st serve % throughout the tournament (54 and 53 respectively) but very strong 1st serve efficiency (82 and 86 per cent respectively) made up for it.

What a low volley by Sampras the racquet squarely hitting the surface - usually these are half-volleys. Still Lendl reacted in time and should've made that though his risk was certainly justified as Sampras would've put away a weaker attempt.
This is what decline looks like - seems almost as good as ever but then a sudden loss of aim results in three quick unforced errors and there's the break.
Sampras profile: Strengths: 1st serve return of serve; Weakness: concentration lapses. Well put.
Some applause for Lendl. The audience must be rooting for the match to become more interesting.
Lendl profile: Strengths: baseline power 1st serve; Weakness: net play.
Perfect depth on that serve almost hit the line.
Lendl guessed right but still had to thread the needle and that he did.
Video feed was taken by the replay of the previous point.
And another one - I'm realising Sampras's half-volley is a totally underrated shot.
Certainly the best game of the match in hindsight. Lendl made some impressive passes and difficult returns but Sampras was clutch and so agile on those half-volleys.

Lendl amusingly complains about a balloon hovering high in the sky claiming it's a distraction. Sampras doesn't say anything but the incredulous look on his face gives away his tacit support - what the hell is that balloon doing here? The ATP supervisor (introduced as Eduardo Menga) comes out personally and tells Lendl they can't do anything about it so he has to play. Ivan is visibly unhappy but being a rational man accepts the obvious truth without much ado - this isn't the sort of bad call he likes to argue over there really is nothing to be done here.
Applause mixed with booing. Lendl really thrived on antagonising the audience as well as his opponents - no better way to do that than make a fuss about something.
Lendl struggling to handle the low slice.
Terrific return great agility to react in time and reflex that strong serve back.
Not sure if Lendl touched the ball or not. Either way awesome angled serve.
A spectacular pass draws crowd cheers.
Again Sampras gets out of trouble with three consecutive 1st serves also earning a round of applause.
The video feed is once again busy showing a fact sheet rather than the serve so this is a gap that will never be filled I guess.
Sampras gets wrongfooted on return yet still manages to chip it far back so Lendl can't attack - nice job. Eventually Lendl wins with a forehand approach that nearly clips the baseline.
A cannonball backhand pass by Lendl makes the audience erupt in cheers - clearly they want the old dog to fight back.
A strangely poor game by Pete for no apparent reason (a concentration lapse as the report said) and Lendl is poised to take the set.
Lendl's rigid volley gives Sampras the opportunity to unleash the pass. Good fightback how will Ivan respond?
Sampras steps back to ensure he makes the return but it sits up and Lendl blasts a heavy forehand to force the error.
Apparently recorded as an ace but I think Lendl just touched the ball.
What an angle on that ace.
Lendl breaks Sampras's rhythm by taking the last ball extra early drawing an error.
Another no-margin half-volley by Sampras. He gestures with the racquet to apologise for the net cord.
Superb slice lob just high enough so Pete can't hit the jumping overhead.
Forces an attackable ball and nets it.
Lendl just doesn't have the consistency anymore - sad to see. Although credit to Sampras for making those deep returns forcing Lendl into neutral rallies.

The first serve was very close to the line; Sampras certainly thought it was in and gave the linesman and the umpire a hard stare. It didn't change the umpire's mind but affected Sampras's own who would suffer another lapse and lose four points in a row.
Great mobility on that return and an excellent corner-deep volley to close it.
Frustrated Lendl kicks the 2nd ball out. Oh well now the match is as good as done.
Amazing return game shame Lendl's service game left him by this point.
Sampras retaliates with a perfect FHDTL of his own. So much power in that shot!
Lendl made some very deep shots and still couldn't hit through Sampras outlasting him in the end.
Sampras hadn't hit a single forehand volley down the line until now - shows a great presence of mind deviating from the usual pattern in crunch time to leave Lendl flat-footed.
Lendl flings his racquet. He's cooked now stamina is not what it used to be.

Sampras was inches away from losing to Woodforde in 3R as the Australian's volley sailed barely out on match point. Pete won the match 2-6 7-6(8) 6-3 and ended up taking the title. A game of millimetres...
Great drop volley on the stretch.
A big forehand to bring up triple BP.
Finally Edberg wins a point on his serve.
That serve was actually long but Pereira won't overrule a call on the far sideline. Besides it would've been silly of Edberg to complain about his own serve not getting called out.
Great first serve but the foot fault couldn't have been more obvious. Luckily Sampras overhits the 2nd serve return anyway.
Smart direction - Edberg expected it crosscourt.
Great half-volley followed by an awesome drop volley peak tennis here.
A monstrous kick serve Edberg nearly had to jump.
In situations like these people say 'what an awful match' but it depends on which way you look at it.
Edberg in danger of winning his first game here.
Edberg hits a slow and low approach off Sampras's low slice giving Sampras time to make a pass but making it difficult to hit it big. Sampras tries and just fails to clear the net.
Edberg with a lob volley a very rare shot.
Excellent passing shot winner to save a set point.
A short dip costs Sampras a break but he immediately regroups and it has no effect on the match.

Edberg thought the return was going out but changed his mind at the last minute (wrongly: the ball would've landed about a foot wide) which produced a weaker volley that Sampras punished with a beautiful lob.
Edberg didn't expect that at all.
What an amazing Sampras slice as the ball was almost behind him. So agile.
Edberg stayed back on the 2nd serve but it kicked high enough to force a backhand error.
That slam dunk is freaking ferocious.
Edberg mostly staying back to mix it up hmm.
A couple of inches wide - shame would've been a terrific pass.
Another very close call elicits a few boos from the crowd.
What a slice by Sampras again.
A wayward 2nd serve seals the deal. Going from 'should've held right there' to 'break point Sampras' certainly rattled Edberg.
Edberg steps back to take on Sampras's serve but Pete deliberately throws a weaker one to confuse Edberg which he does as the Swede misplaces the return.
Weak serve right into Lendl's strike zone and he blasts the forehand.
Big forehands by Lendl keep coming.
Amazing angled backhand by Chang to force the error.
Great depth on Lendl's last two shots.
Great deep volley inviting Chang to risk it.
The difference in FH and serve is decisive despite Chang's better movement and stamina.
These kick 2nd serves are really tough great job by Chang to make decent returns.
Both players have been showing impressive tennis other than Chang's forehand tending to break down under prolonged pressure.
Awful miss Chang got a bit too close to net.
Chang actually got to that ball and it would've been a net cord winner for him if Lendl's shot wasn't out.
Chang is hitting some pretty good slice serves of his own but Lendl handles them fine.
First winner of the match for Chang.
Lendl pacifies Chang with slices until a particularly low one draws an error.
Lendl demonstrates that aggressive baseline play could actually be detrimental against Chang who absorbs the pace so well.
Huge DTL forehand on the run forcing Chang to move back and slice because he had no time.
Lendl changes his racquet during the changeover break.
The lack of penetration in Chang's FH is painfully obvious.
Extreme footspeed from Chang incites loud cheering.
Bad 1st serve call should've been an ace.
Perfect slice low and angled to the max.
Another bad call pathetic officiating. Chang makes it clear: I mean even if it's a fault it's long. That was not wide.
Lendl's net play has been surprisingly high quality.
Paid the price for a meek approach.
Lendl's 'hit to my BH' bait was far too obvious.
Chang's serve lost all bite only placement keeps it any good.
What a low volley from Chang.
Shouldn't have hit it back to Lendl.
Chang whacks the net as if blaming it for the tough net cord.
Code violation: verbal abuse - Warning Rosset

This is the first big tournament Lendl plays as a US citizen. Another curio is that the final was held the following day (Saturday) in order to give the players more breathing room before the Olympics which was just around the corner.
Forced a floater but misdirected the finishing forehand.
Solid low half-volley giving a tough ball despite the slower speed.
Pure power tennis with a textbook volley at the end.
Lendl remains formidable when on song.
Lendl baits Masur into hitting big but Masur doesn't miss.
Lendl thinks the serve was long but doesn't make a fuss as he's leading anyway. Looked long to me too.
Another mean slice return by Lendl.

Lendl goes to the towel table to towel the face and the racquet handle - ah the times when ballkids hadn't yet been made towelkids as well - meaning he goes over the 25 seconds limit which the commentators stress repeatedly in apparent disapproval. The days when that rule garnered genuine respect rather than being abused by all and sundry with extreme umpire leniency are sadly over...
Impressive fight in a hopeless position I say!
One does not simply wrongfoot Ivan Lendl but Masur managed that here.
Lendl lets out a nasty yell.
A very good skidding slice from Masur but Lendl eats it up with an amazing crosscourt bullet.
Lendl returns a big serve and Masur doesn't handle the pressure.
Laver <...> won two Grand Slams I guess that's not too bad. Using the term 'Grand Slam' properly something we rarely hear these days.
Super deep slices wouldn't even fault Masur for the error.
Lendl goes for a precise winner and barely misses.
Point was replayed after problem with net cord sensor
Point was replayed after overrule on first serve
Play suspended due to rain- resumed next day at 4:10 PM
What an amazing start from Lendl; awesome in the literal sense as well.
Lendl is really aggressive today; stepping in and taking the ball early. He usually likes to hover around or just behind the baseline; but today he's really taking the ball early.
Looks like Lendl has left the 'everything goes in' mode; but he's up a break already; so coasting on serve is enough.
The reverse angle shows the return catching the line; and Lendl; just full of confidence at this stage; goes for a clean winner and makes it!
Finally a great point by Edberg.

Edberg moving halfway forward from the baseline after hitting a great angled backhand; and then volleying from the service line and moving to net; results in a volley approach shot. Quite a rarity; and takes superb skills to pull off and win the point.

Edberg thought his 1st serve was an ace - even the commentators thought so - but would rather not argue with the umpire. Still; it clearly bothered him; and two quick errors followed to bring up deuce.
In the last six years; Edberg has won more matches - 424; to be precise - than any other player.
Lendl's smash goes straight at Edberg; who fends it off impressively with sheer reflexes; but still loses the point.
Edberg changes his racquet after double-faulting.
[Stefan Edberg first four rounds: 92 winners at net.]
And Lendl should go to his bag and change racquets; as he usually does at the ball change; and in fact; he's going to do that. The routine he rigidly sticks to.
Excellent defence at net by Edberg. Had to volley low on return and the next shot; yet put the ball deep; then volleyed it away on a change of direction.
Lendl responds like a champ; respect.
For some reason the Lendl fans are more numerous/active this time. There's a lot of I-van! I-van! between the games; and not a lot of the usual Ste-fan Ed-berg! chant.
[Stefan Edberg first four rounds: 76 backhand errors.]
Lendl's 84% 1st serve win has been the key stat so far; but now the match is about to turn upside down.
This might be the key moment when he's serving for a two sets to love lead. We'll see.
Apparently someone in the stands took a flash photo during the point; which distracted Lendl.
A plane flies low over the court just as Edberg is about to serve; forcing him to abort his service motion and start anew.
[Stefan Edberg first four rounds: 6 double faults.]
Really wasn't an approach shot; but when he saw he had his opponent stretching; moved in anyway.
Edberg moonballing Lendl on the forehand side again and winning the point; amazing.

Lendl is showed picking up the racquet he's thrown away in a momentary fit of rage. Nobody expected such a turnaround; least of all Lendl himself. Edberg will ride the wave of confidence now for another set.
Angry Lendl hitting the ball out HARD; eliciting some boos from the crowd. Lendl [is] lucky; I think; not be given a ball abuse warning there.
Edberg lets out a rare cry of frustration; having missed triple BP twice in a row.
Lendl threw a sudden deep floaty backhand for a change of pace/spin; and Edberg didn't adjust well enough.

Lendl mistook the squeal of Edberg's shoes (rubbing against the hard surface when he adjusted his return position) for the double fault alarm and stopped playing; although it would've been tough for him to reach the angled return anyway. The umpire confirmed the alarm did not go off; so Lendl had to accept it was his own fault.
Poor move by Lendl; volleying deep shots is not his game.
The ball might have well been in; but there was no disputing close calls; of course.
Lendl's netcord jumps high and lands right on the baseline; but the lineswoman erroneously calls 'out'. The umpire corrects the call immediately and orders the point to be replayed; as per protocol.
Lendl checking the service line and giving a long hard look to the area where the serve landed; wondering if it was actually a double fault. Looked like it just touched the line.
A fairly poor approach; but incredible movement at net wins Edberg the second successive point. The crowd applauds heartily.
Funny: rival fan groups competing whose chant is louder; I-van! or Ste-fan!.
Edberg trying to surprise Lendl with the drop shot approach; but it's a bit too deep; and Lendl responds with a slice that lands on the sideline. Excellent stuff.
Great backhand winner from outside the court. The crowd is roaring.
Quite fittingly; Edberg's run of 18 consecutive service points won ends on a double fault.
Lendl gets his first lob winner; I think. He doesn't let Edberg's hold streak get into his head.

Edberg throwing moonball forehands again until Lendl mistimes the high slice. It's still funny; considering Edberg's image as a very attacking player; which he was; but that doesn't mean he couldn't push on defence.
Suddenly Lendl produces a great slice return like he hasn't done since the previous set.
Some great kick 2nd serves from Edberg recently; like this one.
A tough low chip return from Lendl; but Edberg executes a supreme half-volley.

The lineswoman mistakenly calls 'out' too early; then corrects herself right away; but the point still has to be replayed; of course. Lendl tells her to 'let it bounce first'. As the commentator explained; the serve was actually starting out wide; but with a lot of spin it curved inside the line.
...Edberg is probably still on the way up or approaching his peak; and Lendl probably just passed his. There has never been a time when clueless comments were not a thing; has there?
Huge mishit by Lendl. The volley was high; allowing great time to adjust and swing freely - and he just botched it. Looks like Lendl's game is about to go south.
Superb backhand flick from Lendl; just a bit too high/late to be called a true half-volley; but still very impressive.

Lendl is done physically; the Australian heat has drained him. He is nearing the end of his prime and doesn't have the same endurance as even the year before; when he was able to outlast Edberg in the fifth set. A point like this one; trying to volley in no-man's land; shows that Lendl has effectively given up. Nothing wrong with it - coming back from this position is impossible when your opponent is clearly fresher. All that's left is get the game of honour; avoiding a shameful bagel; and be done with it.
Ivan Lendl has really played some fine tennis in this match; but in patches - terrific for a set and a half; strong fourth set...
Might have been a second serve
Nimble Edberg too much for Lendl who's not having a great day for sure.
An excellent get off a huge serve leaves Lendl dumbfounded. Way to go!
A baseline-deep return that forces Lendl to backpedal too much ending up in an awkward position to hit the ball.
Good return dipping low so Edberg has to volley up.
...for his serve he [Lendl] bounces the ball four times before his first serve three times on his second. The way it should be.

Edberg is moving much better than Lendl in this match it's clear why he won so easily. Lendl is still strong but past his best while Edberg is at his absolute peak achieving the most dominant of his six major wins.
A bit clumsy on the volley and the smooth Swede threads the needle.
Lendl has to come up with several top notch shots in a row to take the point at last.
The wind makes a good slice tough to deal with. Lendl gets the upper hand this time hitting a really low slice that Edberg uncomfortably overhits.
Annoying kicker though not very deep so Lendl could've handled it.
Wonderful depth on that slice approach Lendl couldn't have done much.
A terrible pass attempt from Lendl easy down-the-middle ball for Edberg to put away.
Low slice forces Edberg to volley up.
Edberg had moved forward in anticipation preparing to chip and charge but his return was too weak and he stayed back which Lendl immediately exploited.
Smart combo of a low slice return forcing Lendl to come forward and a precise passing shot to reap the reward.
Lendl hits a tough low return but Edberg's volley is impeccable.
A great quality point - pacey angled serve mean low return and a superb stretch volley.
Edberg changes racquet after losing three consecutive points on serve.
Stefan's peak agility never ceases to amaze.
Edberg ducks at the last moment and his intuition is right - the ball goes long.
Edberg's first ace of the match comes at a crucial moment.
The crowd goes ecstatic after Lendl plays an awesome behind-the-back shot!
An unexpectedly big serve from Edberg.
Edberg with a playful tweener even though the lob was well out earning some crowd claps. That volley smash was far too careful actually and he's a bit lucky Lendl didn't make that in.
Massive kick yet Lendl nearly got that back.
Lendl's wife not even looking anymore can't bear seeing Ivan so dismantled.
Edberg hits an identical behind-the-back shot to the one Lendl made a few games earlier. Lendl quips wryly I guess anybody can hit that shot. He does have a sense of humour. :)
Nice to hit an ace straight after two lets.
Edberg digs a volley from his shoelaces.
Overhead called in; umpire overrules and calls it out. Connors launches proplonged tirade at umpire
ESampras's strengths: serve & volley; backhand. That was unexpected.
I notice Forget's service motion incorporates a funny left leg twitch.
Sampras is not happy about the call; but Loconto says it's clear; and Pete goes back with a sour expression.
Forget goes for a winner and misses by an inch.
At 85% service games won; Forget is tied for 2nd currently for the '91 season. That's a great stat.
Great body serve; Forget could only manage an awkward weak return.
Loconto makes the 'out' call himself when the linesman does not. Sampras shakes his head.
What a serve! Forget stretches wide; but doesn't even touch it.

Some decent scrambling from Sampras; but really Forget played a pretty bad game. Meanwhile; the bounce is actually quite high - big serves still do the job; but if the return is good; you can expect rallies.
An excellently executed point by Sampras; a low attacking return followed by a gorgeous drop volley.
Forget nearly made that lob; nice defending.
Someone cries from the stands; Come on; Forget! Maybe that fired him up.
Forget lets out a cry; he is dangerously close to getting a virtual bagel.
Exploiting the lefty serve to the backhand; of course.
Forget fooled Sampras by going to the forehand this time;that's what I like; nice mental trickery.
Forget yells; then mumbles something under his breath. He is still in this match.
Again Forget reprimands himself in French.
Finally a great baseline winner from Forget.
Stepped in and hit a bullet; lovely.
Two return winners off Sampras's serve in a row; I bet that didn't happen often.
Great effort from the Frenchman; but Sampras doesn't blink.
Sampras's return seems to hit the net cord judge in the leg. The audience gasps; but the judge; a cosy-looking gray-haired old man; is unharmed.

Forget ends up in an awkward returning position; he still makes the return; then trips and falls; but quickly gets up and raises his hand to tell Sampras that nothing happened; he's alright. The audience claps politely to show appreciation for a moment of niceness.
A great slice serve out wide; almost unreturnable.
Forget does some stretching exercises before the next game to refresh himself.
A double net cord let; that's a rarity (as all shots bouncing off the net more than once are).
Sampras sprints across the baseline and barely gets to the ball; but can't control it.
Lucky that net cord didn't bounce high.
Great stuff! Forget plays his best return point of the match so far to get the mini-break.
And a solid stretch volley to consolidate.
Forget really peaked on the last three points; that's mental strength. Job well done as he takes the tiebreak.

Forget puts the forehand right on the baseline; forcing Sampras to backpedal and overhit. Pete shows displeasure; but doesn't contest a call he knows was right (the ball landed pretty much in the middle of the baseline rather than barely clipping it).
Sampras too hesitant; staying in the middle to handle the incoming return; and Forget exploits that.
A textbook drop volley under pressure.
JOE BRANDI; Pete Sampras' couch. Never heard of him before; good to know.

Sampras hits a careless smash volley off a floating return and is punished with a forehand pass. He can't believe it wasn't called out and; with an impatient Come on!; strolls over to the linesmen with a grumpy look on his face; prompting a round of whistles from the crowd. This Sampras is still young; mature Pete wouldn't let himself get distracted in the heat of battle. -- In fact; as Loconto seems to be considering a time violation warning; Sampras stalls deliberately by dropping his racquet to use both hands to towel his face more thoroughly; and only then he actually gets ready to serve. Probably testing the limits of star/home power here; not that it changes anything.
A round of crowd applause to encourage Pete.
Tough luck for Pete; two returns just barely long.

The serve is called out; but Forget tells the linespeople to give him new balls; indicating that he accepts it was an ace; game Sampras; so it's his turn to serve now. Loconto writes it down in his notebook after Forget confirms it to him again and makes the microphone announcement. Applause ensues - Forget's gesture is well-appreciated.
A mishit return gives Forget an easy opening to attack and score the point.
Another terrific angle on serve; unreachable for Forget.
Sampras outlasts Forget in a 35-second point. I felt for the crowd's collective disappointed sigh when Forget missed the approach shot.
Forget grunts on serve for the first time in the match; and the extra effort pays off as Sampras doesn't adjust well and overhits the return.
Exceptional backhand winner off a low slice.
The American audience moans in disappointment.
The crowd applauds and whistles when the players step back on court with Sampras about to serve to stay in the match; I suppose that didn't help.
Sampras hesitated whether to come in and ended up approaching on a half-volley; making it easy for Forget to earn the point.
The best way to end a match! :D
Lendl stops playing for what he thinks is a disruption but the point is awarded to Chesnokov
Trainer visit to Agassi during changeover
Edberg moonballing on his forehand; that doesn't work against Lendl the powerhouse.

Cunning Lendl taking a step forward after the last FHDTL as if intending to approach the net; but then backing off sideways. Edberg got stuck in 'passing shot' mode; went for a risky angle and netted it.
What a kick serve! No chance to get it.
I love that Lendl didn't even move towards the net; so good was his forehand that it was instantly clear that was going to be a winner.
Please remain seated one more game; play continues. Seats; please. When did they implement a break after every set?
An exquisite slice parallel to the line - one of the most beautiful shots in tennis; I think.
Lendl with a cheeky slice of his own; great stuff to see.
Looks like the sun confused Lendl's vision; because that was a badly misjudged ball.
Nice try; but even with Edberg's hand skills a volley from the baseline is almost impossible to make.
GOAT reflexes at net from Edberg! Instantly redirected Lendl's cannonball. A stunning display.
The point lasted 48 seconds. Great stuff; the men could rally too.
Lendl left the entire court open to hit that forehand; but it was nothing special. The decline in Lendl's groundstrokes is quite clear.
Perfect return that landed in the very corner.
An amazing short-angled forehand from behind the baseline.
Lendl had moved to the right; anticipating a FHCC; and failed to adjust when suddenly he had to hit from the BH side.
Clearly feeling pressured; Lendl makes it a point to complain about the 1st serve call. It looked wide; though; and the umpire is confident telling him this.
Edberg is very somber about this error. Both players are anxious at the moment.
Lendl is very pissed; but again there is nothing he can do. The ball was very close to the line; so this is a call that can't be resolved.
A vicious yell from Lendl is unheard as the crowd erupts in cheers.
Very impressive from the Czech to have channeled his anger into such great play.
Lendl angry again - seems like he wanted Edberg to get foot-faulted; lol. He's been losing his cool in this set. Good mental fortitude to regroup and still win; I guess.

Terrible last four points from Edberg. Overhit a routine volley; double-faulted; netted an easy volley off a floating return; and then hit a toothless 2nd serve on BP that Lendl had no difficulty returning. Can't lose focus like that in tennis...
After netting the shot; Edberg hits the ball out hard in exasperation. Quite unusual for him; showing how frustrated he is at the moment.

Edberg; getting dragged back and forth across the baseline by Lendl's powerful strokes; barely reached that ball and chipped it with the edge of the racquet just over the net - and then Lendl's net cord ball fell on his own side. What a hilarious point.
Edberg hastily changes his racquet; but really his nerves are to blame.
Match length as of match point: 2h 56 min.
Oh dear; wasting another match point with a double fault.
Edberg changes racquet again. Unfortunately; it's not going to help.
Edberg has been standing behind the baseline to return 1st serves. Shows his respect/fear for the Lendl serve; because it's not common for him to back off on return.
A quick Come on! from Lendl. It's been a while since he made a great passing shot; indeed. His confidence is on the upswing after saving two match points.
Bad forehand technique from Edberg; cost him so much career-wise...

Interesting to see Edberg deliberately setting up BH volleys by moving to the right; not the left; when the return comes at his body. He doesn't trust his weaknesses after they failed him in the previous set.
Double faults: Edberg 10; Lendl 2; with 6 of Edberg's 10 DFs coming since *3-4 in the 4th set.
COME ON!; the loudest of them all.
Great drop volley - it's been a while since the last one; too.
Lendl hitting everything super deep; forcing Edberg to run along the baseline. His last forehand was slightly mishit; but Edberg was tired enough to hit it it out anyway.
Edberg testing Lendl's mental clarity with a sudden drop shot; but Lendl kept his focus.
Serious mishit on the 2nd serve; landed almost outside the doubles alley.

Edberg only went to the net twice in the last two games - probably too tired to trust his reflexes anymore. Holds easily anyway; but Lendl is obviously concentrating on holding his own serve. One more hold; and it's over.
The Swedish fan support group is as cheerful as ever; chanting 'Ste-fan Ed-berg!' during the changeover as they always do. Good on them to be so upbeat even as Edberg is losing.
A crucial point is underlined with a mighty Come on! after Lendl forces the error.
The Swedish fans still go another round of chanting Edberg's name; presumably hoping to alleviate the pain of loss and cheer him up a bit. How sweet.
Set 3 video missing but the number of points won should be accurate
1st serve is g  then showing replay
After this point Becker received a Medical Time-Out
Oh dear. Lendl releases his anger by kicking the ball into the air.
Edberg let that high backhand go but somehow it caught a piece of the line.
A perfectly deep body serve (almost touched the service line) is met with an impeccable low return. Edberg does a good job with the volley but still too easy for Lendl's forehand.
Incredible touch such contrast to Ivan's usual power game - love it!
Edberg saves his best serve for the most important point - there's the heart of a champion.
Sublime play by Edberg to get himself out of a tight spot.

Lendl annoyed at lack of calls from the baseline judge (we've seen multiple dubious baseline non-calls for both players already) justly as the replay shows the ball both wide and long and more long than wide at that.

Lendl pretty much orders the umpire to remind the audience that no flashes are allowed during play. Gotta feel good to be a star even if you're rude the officials will still listen as long as you've got a point (and sometimes when you haven't).
What a slice! One of the shots of the match.
Damn so close to a breathtaking return.
Again a superb slice wins Lendl the point.
Lendl with a massive serve but Edberg manages to get it back deep enough and when Lendl doesn't hit the second shot forehand well the Swede quickly takes control and paves his way to winning at net.
That was frightening but not for Stefan apparently.
Painful error could've easily been BP.
The crowd has supported both players quite well but is now largely on Edberg's side.
Edberg is mimicking Lendl with those aces. His confidence must be soaring despite Ivan's consecutive love holds.
The low height of Edberg's slice causes Lendl to overspin the approach allowing Stefan to execute a precise passing shot.
Lendl is struggling with the low slice.
A line-painting return leaves Ivan confused.
Happy cheers every time Edberg wins a point.
Stupendous return here. A lot of crowd cheering despite most of them supporting Edberg that's what being a good tennis fan entails.
Loud excitement from the audience they're loving it and so do I.
Wow Edberg was lucky his first serve didn't go in Lendl's return was a perfect winner.
Edberg with negative DR in a set he won 6-3 what a trick. Clutch job for the new World No. 1 for sure. Well done!

The commie guy droning on about Edberg having better control of his serve now compared to his earlier days - yeah maybe but he's still more prone to double-faulting than your average ATP player. That was always his biggest weakness.
Impressive coordination to get that smash right.
Lendl mishit the pass for a high floater which almost made it more difficult for Edberg who expected a heavy shot - luckily his smash volley landed on the sideline.

Edberg looping the topspin return; inviting Lendl to loop it back; then suddenly slicing the ball very low - that's some skill! - Lendl manages a pretty good slice; but Edberg volleys swiftly into the corner.
Incredible stuff; what a game this is.
An excellent volley on the run here. The crowd is ecstatic.

Edberg's 1st serve % is reportedly 62% (I currently have him at 29/44 = 65;9%; not considering the three missing service games; so good to hear the incompleteness doesn't affect it much). The commentating duo think that's very high for a guy serving this hard.
Love the way this crew here gets the facial expressions right after the rallies of each player. They're on them.

This is a meeting between the top 2 players in the world; Lendl being #1 and Edberg #2. Makes sense why the tennis is so great - serves the occasion right.

A mini-battle on break point: who leaks a weak shot first? The slow-mo replay confirms the ball was just out; so Edberg breaks deservedly.

He's become much more intelligent as a player over the last twelve months.
The cannonball forehand again. Notice how high the ball bounced there. That was shoulder high; perfect for him [Lendl].
Terrific play under huge pressure; every shot was on point. Lendl hit a perfect lob from baseline to baseline; forcing Edberg all the way back; but Stefan saved himself brilliantly.
Edberg trying a big serve with newfound belief; barely missing. His second serve still catches Lendl off-guard; producing a mishit high return that Edberg smashes away.

Oh; I don't believe it! Lendl does not believe it either. He hit two balls as hard as he could. Literally incredible quickness and reflexes from Edberg at net; that was otherworldly. Lendl flings the racquet away while Edberg raises his fist in a heartfelt celebration.

Lendl would rather stay back at this crucial time; as that's his best game. /// Edberg slides and trips on the slippery court.

Right on the line; making the chalk fly up.

Chalk flies up again; pinpoint accuracy.

Lendl appears to have regained his composure during the time-out; and is back to fighting through the match.
A perfect super deep volley under pressure.
Edberg raises hands apologetically and then puts them on the back of his head; astonished at that slice of luck (the net cord volley dropped dead on the other side).
He let it go; Edberg; had a play on that ball.

Edberg drops the racquet on the ground; with an adorably disappointed look on his face that reminds us he is still a teenager.
Quality pass under pressure; parallel to the sideline.

The crowd reacts to Lendl's feisty attitude by giving prolonged cheering to Edberg's next ace.

The crowd outright boos Lendl after he hits the netted ball out. By this point; he has completely antagonised them.

Finally the supervisor comes out and motions for the umpire to announce a weather break. Lendl applauds with his racquet sarcastically to the boos of the crowd.
Some time later; the sky clears up enough for the match to be resumed. Lendl comes out ready to rumble; showcasing his ability with a delightful forehand pass on the run.
Lendl stretches wide for the slice that amazingly touches the line.

Nice to note that both players are given simple chairs to sit during the changeovers; and it's fine. Lendl drinks a little water from the glass brought by a ballboy; Edberg - some tonic beverage from his bottle.
Irritated Edberg hits the racquet against the ground. Again; a reminder that even the beacon of sportsmanship was a little fiery in his youth - but only a little.
Supreme nimbleness and reflexes from Edberg; producing a magical half-volley that completely reverses the point. The crowd roars in delight when Edberg wins it.
A finely calibrated first volley from Edberg against a heavy low angled return. Right into the corner - Lendl could only respond with a lob; then Edberg wrapped it up.
Lendl hits the service line twice in one point: first with his serve; then with the final smash.
Strong coverage of the net by Edberg.
A brave 2nd serve from Edberg here; bounced near the service line.

Lendl didn't expect that Edberg would manage to volley that return back down the line and hesitated for a split second; ended up being a bit too late to the ball to hit a good pass reliably; tried a lob and missed long.
Lendl's face grows gloomier with each game.
Lendl volleys deep; but Edberg is still able to control the ball and set up a pass.
No angry gestures from Edberg; he just looks annoyed.
Probably Lendl's best net point of the match; great defending.
Excellent volleying from Edberg and great athleticism from Lendl; lunging desperately to get that smash back; and it wasn't that far from going in.

Edberg's return jams Lendl and forces a weak half-volley that Edberg hits an easy bullet forehand off - Lendl anticipates the direction correctly and amazingly manages to make a decent volley; but the shot was just too huge.

Lendl hits a safe 2nd serve; but still approaches the net; keeping the intimidation factor. Edberg tries to make a direct return winner and misses by about two inches; then falls to the ground in despair (picking himself up quickly; of course).
Again Lendl takes his time to get ready to serve - that's the mental game.
Lendl's brilliant half-volley lands near the baseline; Edberg; retreating; has a second to think and decides to go for a blistering pass rather than a safe lob; but hits the top of the net.
What a bad miss by Edberg; must be nerves. He drops the racquet in astonishment (and picks it up quickly as well; no antics here).
A very low return forces the error; and it's danger time for Edberg.
Edberg's 2nd serves have been top notch in this match (except that one game with 4 DFs).

More angry actions from Lendl: he throws the racquet on the ground; then catches it by the frame and hits the ground with it again; and again finishes by spitting. No way a player would be allowed to spit on the court so much now.
Great speed from Edberg; although he still couldn't control the lob.
Lendl lunges for the ball and slips pretty badly. The crowd shouts as he gets up; they want to see him lose.
The crowd roars. Match points for Edberg!
Edberg steps back to prepare his swing - and nets it. Tension is in the air.
That was actually a quality 2nd serve; hit deep and bouncing near the service line; but Edberg found a masterful return.

Edberg's sharp return forces a weak volley from Lendl; Edberg runs up to it; Lendl guesses wrong by covering the crosscourt direction and can only watch Edberg's DTL ball fly... and sail out of court. Peak drama now.
Another terrific serve; and Lendl holds after saving three MPs.

Lendl sprints to Edberg's drop volley; bends too far to get to the ball and falls badly on his left knee - that was worse than the previous stumbles. Doesn't injure himself outright; but there's a clear discomfort. He takes time to wipe the chalk off the knee; then slowly goes back to the baseline; bends and stretches his left leg to check whether it's okay. There are shouts from some people in the audience who must think he's wasting time. Lendl; with a smug look on his face; responds by flipping them off with the racquet handle; causing a surprised 'ooh' as well as a few boos; but also some applause - the Aussies like it spicy; ha.
There may be some pain; but clearly no injury as Lendl races along the baseline to retrieve the crosscourt volley.
Lendl changes sweatbands during the break. We can see he's got a slight graze on his left knee.
Caught the very corner of the service box.
This serve bounced off the service line as well.

Chalk flies up... but apparently the ball landed just behind the service line; hence long. Lendl doesn't like it; especially when the umpire tells him it was very long (that's just trolling; dude). Yet this only makes him play better tennis on the next two points.
Classy stuff under pressure from Lendl here.
Looked in to me; but Edberg made no fuss.
Excellent shot quality: a very deep volley into the corner is met with a lob that would've landed near the baseline; had Lendl not caught it with a short angled smash.

A strange drop volley from Lendl - I guess he mistimed it. It was a vertical volley; bouncing high but right near the net. Edberg got there in time; though; and used the sweet disguise of turning his head away from the ball to fake a CC shot while going DTL.
A weak mishit return; and Lendl unleashes the forehand down the line; only for Edberg to guess correctly and hit a beautiful crosscourt backhand winner.

A low return which Edberg does well to volley deep enough; but the ball is weak; so Lendl gets into position and fires the backhand - which would've been a certain winner; since Edberg guessed wrong and moved to the left to cover the CC direction - only it goes long. Lendl doesn't even say or do anything at this point; just looks at the crowd dejectedly.

Edberg gave Lendl a decent opening by making two double faults in this game; but Lendl couldn't make use of the weak volleys his returns forced in the last two points. That was a fatal failure; and now Edberg will break and win.
Lendl rushed that smash - a sign of exhaustion - expecting that Edberg wouldn't be able to get it anyway; but get it he did; and hit a winner. The teenage prodigy is beaming to the hearty applause.
This time Lendl is extra careful with the smash; so Edberg gets a chance but it's still too tough.

A superb angled return; and Lendl still manages to make a good stretch volley; but Edberg races to it and hits a great backhand pass; which Lendl lunges desperately for and falls on the grass one last time.

The umpire announces; Ladies and gentlemen. The final of men's singles championship of Australia; match between J. Connors - J. Newcombe. Best of five sets. Connors has won the toss and elected to serve. ... Linesmen ready. Ballboys ready. Players ready. Play.
Connors had no reason to look happy as he fell down trying to chase the angled return. Not a great start for Jimbo at all.
Great serve - skidded off the line and under Newcombe's racquet as he swung through the air.
Interestingly; the umpire announces Advantage server rather than Advantage Connors. I wonder when that changed.
Rod; if you're watching; best of luck to you in the Las Vegas match against Jimmy Connors in February. Very nice of the Aussie commentator team.
Fun comment here: Unlike previous matches; his [Connors's] shirt is out; and he couldn't care less.
Probably a bad bounce. Connors joking light-heartedly about his great spin - amusing to see the supposed brat in such a jovial mood.
Somebody in the crowd making a smart comment; which Jimmy didn't greatly appreciate. Ha!
Newcombe let the ball go - and it landed right on the baseline.

During the changeover; Connors soaks the handle of his racquet in water and then wipes it clean. The commentators suppose that has to do with the abundance of flies on court; that players have to brush off before serving every so often.
By the way; very nice of the audience to give players mild applause when they leave their chairs to go back on court. Shows their appreciation.

Connors; hoping for the lob to go out; hesitated a bit before running to the baseline; and; as a result; got there too late and missed the smash. His confidence is a bit unsteady; causing an occasional unforced error or a poor decision; which will prove to be crucial in deciding the match.
Connors is so frustrated with the wild miss that he hits himself in the head with his racquet. Could've pressured Newcombe there; instead he's going to get broken now...
A very sweet smash drop shot from Newcombe there.
Although Newcombe lost that exciting exchange; his deep lobs made Connors doubt himself; as seen in the following points.
Connors emits what the commentator aptly describes as the wail of the banshee.
Again Connors guesses wrong. Newcombe really has a fearsome serve when it's on.
Wrongfooting Jimmy even on second serve; masterful.
Newcombe blowing his nose into a handkerchief he kept in his pocket as he walks back to the baseline. Tennis was really cosy back then!

Some more light-hearted banter on court between the two; much to the crowd's amusement. But being too soft probably contributed to Connors's loss in the end. I guess that's why he would later put up the brat act to win.
Cheeky smash drop shot from Connors there.
Amazing volley off even a weak smash!
Commentators during the changeover: Newcombe says he was seven pounds overweight when he started the tournament.
Connors smiling and shouting I can't get that one; too! when he sees the smash go past him.
Connors is taking a lot of time; he's slowed down his service preparation.
An audible Ah; dammit! from Connors.
Connors puts on an angry show - I can't get that! is followed by a racquet throw. Picking it up; he makes a belated 'Very good!' acknowledgement; prompting some giggles from the crowd.

The commentating team giving a great deal of praise to Newcombe's SF win over Roche - 11-9 in the fifth after coming back from 2-5; saving 4 MPs. Apparently Newcombe was so immersed in the match he didn't remember he saved match points until they told him.
Lucky shank for Newcombe; but Connors gets a lucky net cord of his own.
Cat and mouse? More like claycourt tennis.
This match is completely 50/50. Indeed it is - not only are the players one break & set apiece; they both stand at 80 points won right now. The next game will prove to be crucial...

A questionable call. Newcombe gives a long hard look to the linesman and then the umpire; but doesn't say anything yet. The commentators think the ball was probably out - looked suspicious to me as well; but there was no disputing calls back then.
Newcombe is skeptical after the previous call; but it's clearly a bit long this time. Connors mockingly spreads his arms wide to show how 'big' the distance between the baseline and the ball was.

The crowd's applause quickly turns into an uproar as Newcombe signals great indignation by putting a palm over his face; then holding it close to his racquet; indicating how long he thought the ball was. There are shots of 'Fault!' and general whistling while Newcombe mumbles annoyedly under his breath; and Connors is just standing there akimbo with a thoughtful look. The umpire; untouched (as is his duty); announces mildly: 'Forty-fifteen... Forty-fifteen!'; which is met by a wave of booing from the stands (with one woman very loudly shouting 'Oh - my - God!'; funny); as Newcombe and Connors walk back to their returning/serving spots; respectively. Great atmosphere for a Slam final; ha.

Even though the last one was probably a good serve (the commentating team agrees); the one at 0-15 probably wasn't; and Jimmy; who is apparently feeling much too jovial today; decides to throw in an intentional double fault to appease the crowd; which responds with excited cheering and lasting applause until Connors gestures for them to stop. Won't keep some from distracting him later; though. I think that was too kind of Connors - he got soft and thus distracted himself (losing some of the crucial mental focus); gave Newcombe mental advantage; and showed that crowd reaction could pressure him into self-defeating decisions. No wonder he got broken afterwards. I fancy that must have been a big lesson for Jimbo going forward. Still a great match; anyway.

Connors continues to flirt with the crowd; making a funny gesture after missing the first serve - only for some boor to suggest 'Double fault!' as he is about to hit the second. Finally the umpire intervenes and tells spectators to be 'quiet; please'; but the damage is done already.
Newcombe making very intelligent use of the wind that hinders Connors's power game.
Although Connors was certainly rattled; the last three points were all great from Newcombe; so he deserved that break.
Both players often bounce the ball just once or twice before serving - great to see.

Sedgman (as part of the commentator trio) is asked to deliver an opinion as a former pro player; and says that it is common to respect the umpire's decision; especially in a big match - throwing points away deliberately is not viewed as an obligation.

The trick shot from Newcombe was a no-look lob with his back to the court - quality stuff! // ...Game Connors. He leads 5 games to 3. Baffled silence makes the umpire realise his mistake. Correction. Newcombe leads 5 games to 3. A round of applause ensues. Connors seems slightly irritated.
The commentators count 9 aces and 5 doubles for Newcombe; 3 aces and 0 doubles for Connors. Apparently neither the controversial ace nor the intentional double fault that followed are included.
The crowd is firmly behind Newcombe now. A disappointing 'Aww!' when he nets that volley.
Newk let himself be softballed. An interesting way of putting it.
The crowd produces a mighty roar of delight.
This match is being played in remarkably fine spirit. Credit to both players.
Both players regularly have to brush flies away from the face; especially Connors. Unthinkable to allow such a hindrance on court now.
Connors yells in frustration after missing the last shot; then shakes his head irritably. Not so jovial now; naturally.
Observation: Newcombe always gets up from his chair a bit earlier than Connors at the end of the changeover.
Awfully struck serve. Love the commentators' blunt honesty. They also called Connors's backhand return 'glorious'; so no lack of praise for him either - all fair.
A deafening roar and lasting applause from the audience; they are totally into it.
Newcombe takes extra time before serving to brush off flies. Probably a bit of stalling; but really flies have been bothering the players throughout the whole match.
Newcombe even jumped in exasperation when he saw the volley land wide; that's how badly he wanted it over.
Newk slipped and fell in vain chase; then took some time to get up and pull himself together before another service point. Wasn't hurt; just grazed.
The crowd cheers loudly in awe of Connors's resistance. As the second commentator Colin Long put it; the last shot was a bullet-like shot; hit with complete abandon for the winner.
Completely wrongfooted Connors again on those two aces; superb disguise.

Usually the players were just given a glass of water every changeover; but apparently Connors also requested tea and received a teapot and a cup on a teatray the ballboy put beside his chair - that's nice. // Both players made sure to towel the handle of their racquet dry before going back on court.

The umpire; as well as the commentators; calls it a 'tiebreaker' rather than a 'tiebreak'. While both words remain in use as of yet; I think official announcements only use ' tiebreak' now; so it's an interesting point to observe.

Right into the corner; but a mere centimetre wide. Connors playfully makes as if he were petrified by that miss; falling to the ground in despair; then gets up and gazes longingly towards the spot where the ball bounced. The fate of the match is decided by the smallest margins; as befits a great contest.
The elated crowd gives Newcombe a minute-long standing ovation - the umpire can't even finish stating the scoreline! Only gets to 'seven-five'.
